title: InstallZero catalog entry, version 1
description: One known install failure: where it shows up, how to recognise it, what it means, what the user should do, and which named fix the installer may apply. One entry per file, named <id>.json.

id.description: Stable kebab-case id; must equal the file name without .json.

version.description: Bumped when the pattern or fix changes, so failure records refer to an exact entry. Default 1.

order.description: Entries are tried in ascending order and the first match wins. Leave gaps (10, 20, ...) so entries can be inserted. Entries without an order are tried last.

phases.description: Phases whose output this entry applies to, or "*" for all.

pattern.description: .NET regular expression matched case-insensitively against the phase's captured output.

seen.description: Optional .NET regular expression applied from the match onwards; its last match becomes the line shown to the user (e.g. the exception line at the end of a traceback).

requires.description: Optional machine fingerprint conditions, e.g. { "gpu.vendor": "nvidia" }. Reserved; not evaluated yet.

diagnosis.description: What the failure means, in plain language for the user.

advice.description: What the user should do, in plain language.

fix.description: A named fix action implemented by the engine. Entries can never contain commands.

samples.description: Real, redacted log lines. The self-test requires each to match this entry and no earlier one in every listed phase.

source.description: Where the entry came from: curated by a maintainer, proposed by the doctor, or promoted from field records.

records.description: Ids of the failure records that justified a doctor-proposed or field-promoted entry.
